name: Todd Wanek
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2016)
forbes_bio: Todd Wanek is the CEO of Ashley Furniture, the largest home furniture manufacturer and retailer in America.
His dad, Ron Wanek, started the company in the 1970s with a loan from his father and money he got from selling his home.
After graduating from college, Wanek and his new wife Karen spent five years living in Asia, where he managed the company's factory in Taiwan.
In 1994, Wanek returned to the U.S., but continued to run international operations. He was promoted to chief operating officer in 1996.
Wanek has been CEO since 2002; his dad, also a billionaire, remains chairman of Ashley Furniture.
forbes_facts: During high school and college, Wanek held a number of odd jobs at Ashley, including helping on the production line and shipping furniture.
Wanek's son, Cameron, began working for Ashley Furniture in 2015 after receiving an MBA from High Point University.

name: Bradley Jacobs
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2018-2020)
forbes_bio: Most of Bradley Jacobs' fortune comes from XPO Logistics, a commercial transportation company that ships heavy goods like washing machines to homes.
Jacobs created XPO Logistics in 2011 and has expanded it with some $8 billion in deals; he owns just under 18% of the NYSE-listed company.
In the 1990s he consolidated rural trash hauling, building United Waste and flipping it to Waste Management in 1997 for $1.9 billion.
He then built United Rentals into the biggest heavy equipment rental company in the world. Its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
forbes_facts: A trained classical pianist, Jacobs studied piano and mathematics at Brown University before dropping out.
Jacobs has a Palm Beach mansion a few doors down from Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago.

name: Rajeev Juneja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Rajeev Juneja is managing director and vice chairman of Mankind Pharma, which he cofounded alongside his older brother Ramesh Juneja in 1995.
The company sells generic drugs including antibiotics and treatments for cardiovascular diseases in over two dozen markets worldwide.
Ramesh Juneja's U.K.-educated son Arjun is the company's chief operating officer. He led Mankind's entry into international markets, including the U.S.
The company also makes popular brands of condoms and pregnancy test kits.
forbes_facts: Juneja and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart.
Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.

name: Sebastian Glaser
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Sebastian Glaser is the majority shareholder of Sick AG, a world leader in sensor technology.
His grandfather Erwin Sick, an optical engineer, founded the firm in 1946, using earnings from selling radios he made himself to support his family.
After the death of Erwin in 1988, his wife Gisela became the company's primary shareholder and installed external managers.
Active globally with more than 50 subsidiaries, Sick AG now employs around 10,000 people and has annual sales exceeding $2 billion.
Used in factory, logistics and process automation, its technologies are used to measure, locate, inspect and identify.
forbes_facts: After World War II, the American military in Munich granted Erwin Sick a license to set up own engineering firm, which became Sick AG.
Sebastian Glaser serves as managing director of the family's Sick Holding GmbH.

name: Satish Mehta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Pharma distributor's son Satish Mehta founded and runs generics maker Emcure Pharmaceuticals, headquartered in Pune city.
He started Emcure as a contract manufacturer for multinationals in 1981 then went on to sell his own branded generics.
After getting investors such as Bain Capital, he listed the company at a 31% premium in July 2024.
Daughter Namita, an MBA graduate from the Fuqua School of Business and a trained chartered accountant, has a board seat. She's a judge on the Indian version of Shark Tank.
Son Samit, who has an MBA from Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, is also a director on Emcure's board.
forbes_facts: Mehta's son-in-law and nephew work with him.

name: Sergei Gordeev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025)
forbes_bio: Sergei Gordeev is an investor in startups including Hyperloop One, a U.S. highspeed-travel startup.
In 2022 Gordeev resigned as CEO of PIK SZ, the biggest Russian real estate developer where he has about 60% shares.
In 1995, he founded Rosbuilding, which bought shares of different plants.
He bought a 20% stake in home builder PIK from billionaire Suleiman Kerimov in 2013, and eventually became the controlling shareholder.
He made his fortune buying up shares of industrial companies in Moscow and then turning factories into office complexes.
forbes_facts: Gordeev, who is interested in architecture, designed his own house in a London suburb.
Gordeev bought a factory once owned by a theater director, founded a theater there and for many years sponsored its troupe.

name: John Oyler
sec_insider_companies: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (ONC) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John Oyler is the CEO, cofounder and chairman of global oncology company BeOne Medicines. He owns nearly 5% of the publicly traded company.
BeOne Medicines, which was formerly called BeiGene, was founded in 2010 as a research and development firm. It went public on the Nasdaq in 2016 and listed in Hong Kong two years later.
Before he cofounded BeOne, Oyler helped start and then sell two companies in the U.S. and China.
He sold Telephia, a consumer telecom research firm he founded in 1997, to The Nielsen Co. for $449 million in 2007.
Oyler's next success came with drug discovery outsourcing company BioDuro, which he founded in 2005 and sold to PPD Inc. for $77 million in 2010.
forbes_facts: BeOne has more than 40 drugs in its pipeline. Its blood cancer drug Brukinsa did more than $2 billion in U.S. sales in 2024.

name: B. Wayne Hughes Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: B. Wayne Hughes Jr. was born into the self-storage business; his father, B. Wayne Hughes (d. 2021), cofounded Public Storage in 1972.
Hughes Jr. worked at Public Storage for almost two decades, starting in 1983.
He was vice president of acquisitions from 1992 to 2002 and served on the board until late 2020.
In 2005 he launched American Commercial Equities, a real estate company that acquires and manages properties in Hawaii and California.
His Hughes Charitable Foundation focuses on issues such as education, at-risk youth and food and housing insecurity in his home state of Wyoming.
forbes_facts: Hughes Jr. is the founder of Serving USA, a nonprofit that helps military families, victims of crime and former inmates rebuild their lives.
Hughes Jr.'s sister, Tamara Hughes Gustavson, is also a billionaire.

name: Anurang Jain
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2016-2022)
forbes_bio: The late motorcycle tycoon Rahul Bajaj's nephew Anurang Jain started Endurance Technologies in 1985 to supply aluminum castings to his uncle's Bajaj Auto.
Jain owns a majority stake in Endurance, which supplies parts for two-wheelers and three-wheelers in India and car parts in Europe.
Endurance has 18 factories in India and 9 in Europe.
Jain made news when he bought two apartments in 2020 for $14 million in a Mumbai luxury high-rise, close to Mukesh Ambani's residence.
forbes_facts: Jain's twin Tarang runs his own auto components firm called Varroc Engineering.
Their father Naresh Chandra was chairman of both the companies but retired in 2020.

name: Alex Birkenstock
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Alex Birkenstock is an heir to German footwear company Birkenstock, which traces its roots back to 1774.
The company began making its trademark sandals in the 1960s, under the leadership of Alex's father, Karl Birkenstock.
In 2002, Alex and his two brothers, Christian and Stephan, were given control of the company.
Stephan Birkenstock sold his stake to his two brothers in 2013 for an undisclosed amount.
In 2021, the brothers sold Birkenstock to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's holding company for more than $4.5 billion. Christian rolled forward a stake then worth $300 million.

name: Oran Holtzman
sec_insider_companies: Oddity Tech Ltd (ODD) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Oran Holtzman and his sister Shiran Holtzman-Erel founded Oddity Tech in 2018, a data-driven company that develops and sells beauty products online.
Holtzman is the chairman and CEO of the more than half-billion-dollar (2024 revenue) company; Shiran is the Chief Product Officer.
Oddity brands virtually match consumers to a makeup or skincare product using AI and software technology.
The company's two brands, Il Makiage and SpoiledChild, sell directly to Oddity's more than 50 million customers solely online.
Oddity debuted on the Nasdaq in 2023 at a $2.7 billion market cap.
